statement: a certificate (epsilon_bound, K_epsilon, P_height, P_ineq, P_finiteness) implies the abc conjecture

premises.note: rad(n) is well-defined and multiplicative for coprime inputs (spec §1.1)
abc conjecture: for all epsilon>0 there exists K_epsilon such that for all coprime a+b=c: c < K_epsilon * rad(abc)^(1+epsilon) with finitely many exceptions (spec §1.1)
certificate = (epsilon_bound, K_epsilon, P_height, P_ineq, P_finiteness) as in spec Definition 1

proof_steps.label: unfold-abc-conjecture
proof_steps.claim: abc conjecture for epsilon := (for all coprime a+b=c: c <= K_eps * rad(abc)^(1+eps)) except finitely many
proof_steps.justification: Direct unfolding of Definition 1 of the abc conjecture (spec §1.1). Finitely many exceptions are allowed.

proof_steps.label: unfold-certificate-P_ineq
proof_steps.claim: P_ineq in the certificate is a universal statement: for ALL coprime a+b=c, c <= K_eps * rad(abc)^(1+eps)
proof_steps.justification: Certificate definition (spec Definition 1, §1.2): P_ineq must be a universal bound over all coprime triples, not agreement on a finite collection (spec §2.1, B3).

proof_steps.label: unfold-certificate-P_finiteness
proof_steps.claim: P_finiteness in the certificate proves: {(a,b,c) coprime, a+b=c : c > K_eps * rad(abc)^(1+eps)} is finite
proof_steps.justification: Certificate definition (spec Definition 1, §1.2): P_finiteness provides the finiteness of exceptions.

proof_steps.label: identify-components
proof_steps.claim: The conjunction of P_ineq (universal bound with finitely many exceptions) exactly matches the abc conjecture statement for this epsilon
proof_steps.justification: Definitional substitution: step 1 = conjunction of steps 2 and 3.

proof_steps.label: conclusion
proof_steps.claim: Given a certificate (epsilon_bound, K_epsilon, P_height, P_ineq, P_finiteness), the abc conjecture holds for epsilon = epsilon_bound
proof_steps.justification: Substitution from step 4: the certificate directly witnesses the abc conjecture for this epsilon. No construction leaves used — this is purely definitional.

non_circularity: The proof is purely definitional. No abc triples, no fitted K_epsilon, no Szpiro assumed, no IUT used. The certificate definition was constructed to match the abc statement precisely.
